symbols.name: input sequence
symbols.meaning: The input sequence of the transform, a list of $2r$ ring elements $u_0,\dots,u_{2r-1}$.
symbols.quote: Let $u_0,\dots,u_{2r-1}$ be a sequence of ring elements; here $u$ names a sequence, not the first butterfly input of earlier pages.

symbols.name: second input sequence
symbols.meaning: The second input sequence, a list of $2r$ ring elements $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ whose transform is multiplied entrywise with that of $u$.
symbols.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

symbols.name: transform of u
symbols.meaning: The synthetic transform of $u$, whose entry at frequency $s$ is $\hat u_s$.
symbols.quote: Its transform has entries $\hat u_s=\sum_{t=0}^{2r-1} y^{st}u_t$.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: The input position in $u$, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $t$ be the input position and $s$ the frequency index, $s=0,\dots,2r-1$.

symbols.name: frequency index
symbols.meaning: The frequency index of a transform entry, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $t$ be the input position and $s$ the frequency index, $s=0,\dots,2r-1$.

symbols.name: pair index
symbols.meaning: The index of the pair of frequencies $2i$ and $2i+1$, running over $0,\dots,r-1$.
symbols.quote: Write $i$ for the index of the pair of frequencies $2i$ and $2i+1$, so $i$ runs over $0,\dots,r-1$.

symbols.name: input position in z
symbols.meaning: The input position in $z$, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

symbols.name: output position
symbols.meaning: The index $h$ of an entry $(u\ast z)_h$ of the cyclic convolution.
symbols.quote: Let $u\ast z$ be the cyclic convolution of $u$ and $z$, with entries $(u\ast z)_h=\sum_{t+q\equiv h \pmod{2r}} u_tz_q$, where $h$ is the output position.

relations.quote: It works in the [polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md).
It is built on $y$ as a [primitive root of unity](roots-of-unity.md) of order $2r$: $y^r=-1$, so $y^{2r}=1$, and no smaller positive power of $y$ equals $1$.
A synthetic polynomial transform generalizes the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) to a polynomial ring whose roots of unity are powers of $y$.
